senses.definition: The part of a plant that anchors it and takes in water and minerals. Roots often grow below ground.
senses.example: The carrot’s leaves grew above the soil, and its plant root grew below.

senses.definition: The part of a plant that holds up leaves, flowers, or other parts and carries materials between them.
senses.example: A sunflower has a tall stem.

senses.definition: A small passage in a leaf that carries water or sugars through it.
senses.example: Tiny veins spread outward from the middle of the leaf.

senses.definition: Plant tissue that carries water and minerals from the roots toward the leaves.
senses.example: The tree’s xylem carried water into branches above the roof.

senses.definition: Plant tissue that carries sugars from where a plant makes or releases them to parts that need them.
senses.example: The leaf sent sugars down the phloem to growing roots.

senses.definition: A tiny opening in a plant surface. Water vapor and gases move through it.
senses.example: A microscope showed each stoma on the underside of the leaf.

senses.definition: The release of water vapor from a plant, mostly through its leaves.
senses.example: Transpiration added water vapor to the air around the tree.

senses.definition: A part of a flower that is often brightly colored and surrounds the pollen-making or seed-making parts.
senses.example: Five yellow petals surrounded the center of the flower.

senses.definition: The part that develops from a flowering plant’s ovary and usually contains seeds.
senses.example: A cucumber is a fruit even when you use it in a salad.

senses.definition: To start growing from a seed or spore.
senses.example: A root appeared as the bean seed began to germinate.

senses.definition: A short plant stem with thick layers that store food, often found underground.
senses.example: A tulip bulb can grow a fresh shoot in spring.

senses.definition: A swollen part of a plant that stores food and can grow new shoots in some plants.
senses.example: A potato is a tuber on an underground stem.

senses.definition: A plant stem that grows sideways, usually under or along the ground.
senses.example: New shoots grew at points on the iris rhizome.

senses.definition: A stem that creeps away from a parent plant and can make new plants along the way.
senses.example: The strawberry’s runner reached over the edge of the pot.

senses.definition: A plant that keeps some green leaves throughout the year.
senses.example: The spruce is an evergreen, so its branches looked green in January.

senses.definition: Describes a tree or shrub that drops most of its leaves for part of each year.
senses.example: The deciduous maple was bare in winter.

senses.definition: A tiny cell that can grow into a new living thing in suitable conditions.
senses.example: A fern released spores from spots under its leaves.

senses.definition: Adapted to get food or nutrients by eating animals.
senses.example: A carnivorous plant can catch a fly in a modified leaf.

senses.definition: A living thing such as a mushroom, mold or yeast that gets food by absorbing it from other material.
senses.example: The fungus absorbed food from a fallen log.

senses.definition: The spreading network of fine threads that makes up much of a fungus.
senses.example: Hidden mycelium grew through the damp wood.

senses.definition: A living thing that breaks dead material into simpler substances.
senses.example: A fungus can act as a decomposer after a branch falls.

senses.definition: A partnership in which a fungus grows with an alga or a tiny organism that can make sugars from light.
senses.example: The gray lichen grew on the fence post.

senses.definition: A close partnership where a fungus grows with a plant’s roots.
senses.example: The mycorrhiza helped the young tree get minerals from the soil.

senses.definition: Two or more kinds of material together that can still keep their own properties.
senses.example: Trail mix is a mixture of different foods.

senses.definition: An even mixture formed when one substance dissolves in another.
senses.example: Stirring salt into water made a salt solution.

senses.definition: To spread through another material in particles so small that you no longer see the separate pieces.
senses.example: The sugar began to dissolve in the water.

senses.definition: The amount of one substance that can dissolve in a certain amount of another under given conditions.
senses.example: Heat can change the solubility of sugar in water.

senses.definition: Describes a mixture that already holds as much of a dissolved substance as it can under its current conditions.
senses.example: More salt stayed on the bottom after the water was saturated with salt.

senses.definition: A substance made of atoms from at least two different elements chemically joined in a fixed proportion.
senses.example: Water is a compound of hydrogen and oxygen.

senses.definition: A solid with particles arranged in a pattern that repeats throughout it.
senses.example: Under a magnifier, a crystal of table salt looked like a tiny cube.

senses.definition: A pulling effect at the surface of a liquid that makes its surface tend to shrink.
senses.example: Surface tension helped pull a drop of rain into a rounded shape.

senses.definition: A mixture that holds tiny drops of one liquid spread through another liquid.
senses.example: Shaking the jar formed an emulsion of drops of oil in water.

senses.definition: A change in which substances turn into other substances as atoms rearrange.
senses.example: Tiny gas bubbles marked a chemical reaction in the batter.

senses.definition: A scale used to describe how acidic or basic a water-based liquid is.
senses.example: The colored strip helped us compare the pH of two drinks.

senses.definition: In chemistry, a substance that shows something about a liquid, often by changing color.
senses.example: A pH indicator can change from purple to pink in an acidic drink.

senses.definition: Damage to a material after it reacts with substances around it, such as air or moisture.
senses.example: A coat of paint can protect a steel bridge from corrosion.

senses.definition: A material containing a metal mixed with one or more other elements.
senses.example: Brass is an alloy that contains copper and zinc.

senses.definition: A hard material, such as fired clay, usually made from minerals and set by heat.
senses.example: The ceramic in the cup started as soft clay.

senses.definition: A material made of very long molecules built from many smaller pieces joined in chains or networks.
senses.example: Cellulose, which helps plants stay strong, is a natural polymer.

senses.definition: A thin thread or strand that can be used to make cloth, paper or rope.
senses.example: The sweater was made with fibers from sheep’s wool.

senses.definition: A wet mixture of little fibers used to make paper.
senses.example: The paper machine squeezed water out of the pulp.

senses.definition: A soft form of carbon in which flat layers of atoms can slip past one another.
senses.example: A pencil point leaves some graphite on the page as it moves.

senses.definition: A substance plants make that can help a fruit mixture become thick and soft.
senses.example: Pectin helped the jelly keep its shape on the spoon.

senses.definition: Broken or crushed glass gathered for use when making new glass.
senses.example: The glass plant mixed clean cullet with sand and its other supplies.

senses.definition: A kind of tiny fungus. Bread yeast can use sugars and release carbon dioxide gas.
senses.example: Yeast made bubbles that swelled the bread dough.

senses.definition: A way some living things get energy by changing sugars into other substances.
senses.example: During fermentation, tiny gas bubbles appeared in the bread dough.

senses.definition: To join a piece cut from one plant to a part of another plant so that they grow together.
senses.example: The orchard worker grafted a branch from an apple tree onto another tree’s roots.

senses.definition: A place where many trees are grown for fruit or nuts.
senses.example: We picked several kinds of apples in the orchard.

senses.definition: A small hard seed or fruit from a crop such as corn, wheat, oats or rice.
senses.example: The cook stirred the grains of rice in the pot.

senses.definition: The outer layers of a grain that may be taken off when it is milled.
senses.example: Brown rice still has bran around its lighter center.

senses.definition: A dark mixture formed after scraps from plants and other living things break down.
senses.example: The finished compost was mixed with soil near the flowers.

senses.definition: A covering such as straw or wood chips laid over soil to help hold water or limit weeds.
senses.example: The mulch shaded the soil around the plants.

senses.definition: A frame that a climbing plant can grow on.
senses.example: Pea plants climbed the trellis by the fence.

senses.definition: A slender part of a climbing plant that can curl around something and hold on.
senses.example: A pea tendril curled around the string.

senses.definition: The liquid left when the soft solid parts of milk separate during cheese making.
senses.example: The whey drained away, leaving thick curds behind.

senses.definition: A soft lump of milk solids that can form when milk proteins gather together.
senses.example: The cheese maker gathered the curds into a mold.

senses.definition: Water with dissolved materials that moves through plants, including the sugar-rich liquid collected from some maple trees.
senses.example: Maple sap dripped into the line leading from the tree.

senses.definition: The nut of an oak tree. An acorn has a hard shell and a little cap.
senses.example: An oak seedling grew where a jay had hidden an acorn.

senses.definition: One of the separate parts packed together in a garlic bulb.
senses.example: The cook peeled a clove of garlic.

senses.definition: Growth that bends a plant part toward or away from light.
senses.example: Phototropism turned a seedling’s stem toward the window.

senses.definition: Plant growth that changes direction in response to gravity.
senses.example: Through gravitropism, a root bent downward after the seed changed position.

senses.definition: The temperature at which a liquid starts boiling at a particular pressure.
senses.example: The boiling point of water is lower on a high mountain.

senses.definition: The temperature at which a liquid forms solid crystals under given conditions.
senses.example: Dissolved salt lowered the freezing point of the water.

senses.definition: A thin sheet of wood that can be glued onto something or pressed together with other sheets.
senses.example: The plywood had a smooth veneer on its top layer.
